prompt_text: My roof has hail damage in Denver. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you a targeted list — but I don’t have live web access right now. If you tell me your Denver zip code (or neighborhood) I’ll pull together 4–6 locally available, well-reviewed roofing/repair companies to call. Meanwhile, here’s an immediate, practical plan plus specific kinds of companies you should contact and why.

Who to call first (and why)
- Your homeowner’s insurance company — to report the claim and learn their next steps. Ask whether they require contractor estimates or will send an adjuster first.
- A manufacturer-certified roofer (GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Platinum Preferred, or CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster) — these certifications indicate training, warranties, and quality standards. Certified contractors are more likely to handle hail-specific damage correctly and provide manufacturer warranties.
- A local Denver storm/hail specialist — local firms that handle high-volume hail claims know how to document damage for insurers and understand Denver’s permitting and code requirements.
- A restoration company that works with insurance claims (e.g., Paul Davis Restoration or SERVPRO franchises) — they handle tarping, moisture mitigation, and coordination with insurers when damage is widespread.
- A public adjuster (only if damage is extensive or claim is denied/underpaid) — they act on your behalf with the insurer for a fee.

How to find the right companies (quick searches to run)
- Search for “GAF Master Elite contractors near [your zip]” (or “Owens Corning Platinum Preferred” / “CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster”).
- Search Google/Yelp for “hail damage roof repair Denver” and sort by high ratings + many recent reviews.
- Check BBB.org and Colorado’s contractor licensing records (Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies/DORA or Denver Building Department for local permits) to confirm license and complaints.

Questions to ask every contractor (phone call or visit)
- Are you licensed and insured in Colorado? Can you provide certificate of liability insurance and worker’s comp?
- Do you have experience handling hail claims in Denver? How many hail jobs have you done this year?
- Are you certified by any shingle manufacturers (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed)? Can you show proof?
- Will you provide a written, itemized estimate (materials, labor, permit fees, disposal)? Do you provide a written warranty (labor & materials)?
- Do you assist with insurance documentation/claim process?
- What is your timeline for inspection and for starting/finishing work?
- Who will subsurface-inspect (sheathing, flashing)? Will you photograph damage for the insurer?
- Payment terms; do you require a large upfront deposit? (Red flag: high cash-only deposits or pressure to sign immediately.)

What to look for in written estimates
- Itemized scope (shingles brand and weight, underlayment, flashing, ice/water barrier)
- Removal and disposal of old roof
- Permit details and code compliance
- Start/completion dates and lien waiver policy
- Clean-up and post-job inspection
- Labor warranty (length) and whether manufacturer warranty is transferable

Red flags / scams to avoid
- “Storm chasers” who knock immediately after hail and pressure you to sign right away.
- Contractors who request full cash up front or only accept cash.
- No local office or no local address/phone number.
- Vague estimates (no brand names, no itemized costs)
- High-pressure “pay now or we’ll raise the price” tactics

Emergency steps
- Take many photos (wide shots and close-ups) of hail-damaged roofing, gutters, siding, vents, and any leaks inside.
- If there is active leakage, get temporary tarping. Confirm tarping cost and temporary nature in writing.
- Keep all receipts and communication with insurance and contractors.

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short phone script you can use on calls.
- If you tell me your Denver zip code or neighborhood, I’ll produce a tailored shortlist (3–6) of local firms to call and a recommended first call order based on whether you prefer manufacturer-certified installers, lowest cost, or fastest schedule.

Which of those would you like next? (If you want local names, give me your zip code.)
